newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Aon unit's future unclear as director goes.
newsitem.headline: Aon unit's future unclear as director goes.

text.p: The future of Singapore insurance broker Heath Hudig Langeveldt Pte Ltd (HHL) was unclear on Thursday after fellow Aon Corp unit, Inchcape Insurance Brokers Pte Ltd, was appointed correspondent broker.

Sources close to HHL told Reuters that Aon had sent letters to clients on Thursday saying Inchcape's appointment was "a result of the sudden and unforeseen departure" of HHL managing director Eddie Chua.
The move followed a meeting of Aon directors in Singapore on Wednesday to discuss the impact of the loss of Chua, who was said to have left the company last week.
Reports in the Singapore press last week said up to 20 of the 30-strong team at HHL had also resigned over the past month.

Staff at HHL could not comment on the action, nor could they confirm whether the arrangement was permanent or temporary. Clive Bate, chairman of Aon Holdings Asia Ltd, could not be reached for comment.

Insurance sources close to HHL said Chua had been removed after a dispute with Aon over his minority shareholding in HHL. Relinquishing the stake was thought to have been part of the deal struck by Aon when it bought HHL in late 1995.
Chua could not be contacted for comment. The sources said he was subject to a three-month vow of silence imposed by his former employers.
Industry sources said they expected him to set up a rival insurance brokerage in the near future.
Aon has three direct insurance and one reinsurance broking operations in Singapore. The sources said the disruptions at HHL were unlikely to affect Aon's long-term plans in Asia.
